title: Brar Arrogance Deepens the Rift with the Scattered Singhs

blocks.text: Seeing the Khalsa scattered and weakened after repeated invasions, the Brars turned very arrogant and began taunting the Majhail Singhs instead of helping them. They mocked the refugees' hardship, forgot how often the Singhs had taken shelter in the Malwa region, and treated Sikh vulnerability as a chance for domination.

Their threats soon became openly political as some Brars boasted that they had threatened the Singhs with elimination by inviting Mughal and Pathan authorities. That swagger transforms local insult into something far more dangerous, because it hints that hostility between the scattered Singhs and those powers could be used as a weapon inside Malwa itself.

The page also folds in the provocation around Ganda Singh's household, showing how everyday humiliation and rumor begin to harden into a larger communal breach. What had been tension now starts moving toward deliberate confrontation.
